tasks.spec:
You are probing one untested seam between two components of a patient-booking system. BOUNDARY: write only inside your own task directory. Never modify anything outside it. Never send a message. Never pass --approve or --max-sends to anything. Never git commit. You own exactly two output files: ./report.md and ./dryrun_output.txt.

WHAT IS UNTESTED. A batch SMS sender and a booking gateway have never been run against each other. The sender has 74 passing unit tests, all of which use a fake HTTP layer, so nothing has ever proven the sender can actually reach the gateway, authenticate to it, or understand its answers. Every real defect found in this system this week lived in exactly this kind of seam.

WHAT TO RUN. The sender is /mnt/d_drive/repos/bland/scripts/sms_recall_batch.py and must be run from /mnt/d_drive/repos/bland as the working directory. Its --dry-run mode performs the full read chain and sends nothing: it loads a manifest, loads a send ledger, loads a feed, looks each patient up through the gateway, pulls the gateway's suppression list, applies a frequency cap, and prints counters. Use ./source/mott_outbound_recall_manifest.v1.json as the manifest, copying it into your task directory first if you prefer.

CREDENTIALS. The gateway needs the environment variable MOTT_GATEWAY_TOKEN. Resolve it at runtime only, through the approved wrapper, exactly like this, as ONE line: AWS_PROFILE=deploy-admin python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/finances/scripts/secret_exec.py --secret-env MOTT_GATEWAY_TOKEN=conductor/agents/bland-mott/api-key -- python3 scripts/sms_recall_batch.py --feed <your feed> --manifest <your manifest> --dry-run
NEVER print, echo, log or copy the token value anywhere. If the wrapper is denied with an AccessDenied error, that is a real and useful finding: record it and report the exact error, do not try other profiles more than once each and do not attempt to read the secret by any other route.

THE FEED. Create it yourself with SYNTHETIC values only. Never use a real patient identifier or a real phone number. Use invented numbers in the +1202555xxxx range and invented patient ids such as P900001. The accepted column shapes are defined in the sender; read it and pick one. A synthetic patient will not resolve at the gateway, so expect the row to be dropped by enrichment. THAT IS A PASS, not a failure: the point is proving the sender reaches the gateway and understands the answer, not that a fake patient exists.

CAPTURE the complete stdout and stderr of the dry run into ./dryrun_output.txt, unedited.

WHAT TO DETERMINE AND REPORT: whether the gateway was reachable at all; whether authentication succeeded or failed and with what status; whether the token needed a Bearer prefix that the sender does not add, since the sender passes the environment value through unmodified; what the patient lookup returned for a synthetic id; whether the suppression list call succeeded; the exact value of every counter line the sender printed; and confirmation that external_actions_taken was 0.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md. Start with '# Dry Run Seam Probe'. State one of 'SEAM: PROVEN', 'SEAM: BROKEN', or 'SEAM: BLOCKED' on its own line, where BLOCKED means you never obtained a credential. Then '## Summary' with at most 3 bullets, '## What The Counters Said' as a table of counter name and value, '## Failures Encountered' listing each error verbatim with what it means, '## What This Does Not Prove', and '## Assumptions'. Under 800 words. Be honest if the seam is broken: a broken seam found now is the entire point of this task.

tasks.spec:
You are adding one capability to a live SMS booking pathway: persisting a patient's opt-out. BOUNDARY: write only inside your own task directory. Never modify anything outside it. Never call an API, never send a message, never mint or deploy a pathway, never git commit. You own exactly three output files: ./build_v56.py, ./v56_graph.json and ./report.md.

THE PROBLEM. When a patient replies STOP, or says they are not the person being texted, the pathway thanks them and gives them the office phone number, and writes nothing down. The next campaign texts them again. The endpoint that records an opt-out has existed since 2026-07-25 and no node calls it.

SOURCE MATERIAL. ./source/build_v55.py generates the current graph and ./source/v55_graph.json is its output. ./source/SUPPRESSION-CONTRACT.md is an audited report of the gateway's suppression endpoint, including its exact request contract, its permitted field values, its idempotency behaviour and every failure status it can return. Treat that report as authoritative and read it completely before writing anything.

WHAT TO BUILD. Copy build_v55.py to build_v56.py and change only what this task needs. Insert a silent webhook node in front of EACH of the two opt-out end nodes, so neither can be reached without the call being attempted first. Each webhook posts to the suppression route on the same gateway the other webhooks use, carries the same stored-secret authorization header as every other webhook, sets retryAttempts to 0, and sends exactly the three contracted fields and no others. The phone field must interpolate an existing conversation variable rather than any literal or composed value. Choose the reason and source values from the permitted sets in the contract, picking the ones that honestly describe each of the two situations.

CONSTRAINTS THAT WILL FAIL YOUR WORK IF BROKEN. The endpoint can answer 503 when its storage is unavailable, so a call is not proof a record landed: NO node may tell the patient they have been removed, taken off the list, unsubscribed, or that they will not be contacted again. The existing wording, which points them at the office, is honest and must stay honest. The change must be purely additive: every node that exists in v55 other than the two opt-out end nodes must come out structurally identical, with the same routing conditions, the same extraction variables and the same message text. Do not renumber, rename, retune or improve anything else, however tempting.

Run your build_v56.py to produce ./v56_graph.json in your task directory. Verify your own output before finishing: confirm both opt-out exits have a suppression call as their only inbound route, and diff your node set against v55 to confirm nothing else moved.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md. Start with '# Suppression Wiring'. Include '## Summary' with at most 3 bullets, '## Nodes Added' as a table of node id, what it posts, and which exit it guards, '## Values Chosen' explaining why each reason and source value honestly describes its situation, '## What Stays Honest' quoting the patient-facing wording that must not change and saying why, and '## Assumptions'. Under 700 words.
